transcript.text: Thank you both for being here. As we review the proposal to convert the unused paved courtyard into a science learning garden, I want to make sure we've covered all our bases before I make a final decision. The current plan calls for planting six species directly in the existing soil, starting in September, with three science lessons held in the garden. What I need from each of you is straightforward: is there anything we should be including or addressing before I approve this? Please share whatever concerns or considerations you have.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to flag a critical issue. I received a soil laboratory report yesterday showing lead at 185 parts per million in the courtyard soil, which is above our district's 100-ppm threshold. District procedure requires us to remove the top 8 inches of soil and replace it with certified clean soil before students can use the garden. This report hasn't been added to the project proposal yet — it's still in my facilities folder awaiting weekly review. This needs to be addressed before any approval, and it will affect both the timeline and the budget for September planting.

It also requires exactly 6 science lessons in the garden by November 1, 2026 — not the three currently planned.
